title: Bowel obstruction and ileus in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the bowel obstruction or ileus (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Partial small bowel obstruction.

Vitals:
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 78 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air

Recent Labs:
WBC: 8.4 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 12.2 g/dL
Hematocrit: 37%
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
Electrolytes: Sodium 138 mEq/L, Potassium 4.1 mEq/L

Review of Systems:
The patient reports abdominal pain and bloating. She denies fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting. She denies any changes in bowel habits or urinary symptoms. She denies shortness of breath or chest pain.

Social History:
The patient lives at home with her spouse. She is a former smoker (quit 20 years ago). She denies alcohol or illicit drug use.

Family History:
Mother had hypertension. Father had a history of heart disease.

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 79-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with progressive abdominal discomfort and distension. Imaging confirmed a partial obstruction of the small bowel. The etiology of the obstruction was not identified during the evaluation. She was admitted for conservative management and was started on strict bowel rest and intravenous fluids. During the hospitalization, her symptoms improved significantly. She was able to tolerate a transition to a clear liquid diet and eventually progressed to a soft diet without further complications. The partial obstruction resolved while she was in our care. She was discharged in stable condition.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Partial small bowel obstruction.

Discharge Medications:
1. Lisinopril 10 mg daily
2. Atorvastatin 20 mg daily
3. Multivitamin daily

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a routine evaluation and to monitor for any recurrence of symptoms.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Partial intestinal obstruction, cause not stated: K56.600 (HCC 78).
